title: An elementary twist-ratio bound for the SU(2) Wilson lattice, formalised in Lean 4 on the objects of OpenAI's four-dimensional development and its extension to a cyclic centre (note v1.2)
description:
An elementary twist-ratio bound for the SU(2) Wilson lattice, formalised in Lean 4, and its extension to a cyclic centre (note v1.2, 12 November 2026).

Version 1.2 adds a section on a cyclic centre ZN. For ζ = e2πi/N and q ≠ 0 mod N, the Fourier transforms over the centre twists of the Wilson partition function, &Zcirc;q = ∑k ζqk Zk (the electric-flux projectors of Kanazawa, up to normalisation), satisfy |&Zcirc;q| ≤ ρ|P| &Zcirc;0, with ρ = 1 − e−2κ for every N and every coupling. Sixteen further Lean 4 declarations (namespace CentreZN, importing Mathlib only; the N = 2 case of the published statements is derived from them) are accepted by the Lean kernel (4.32.0 and 4.32.2) and by the independent kernel nanoda, standard axioms only, and were rebuilt by a model that did not write them. On paper only (checked by AI models only): the improvement ρ ≤ tanh κ for all N, closed forms of the optimal constant for N = 3, 4, the corollary for SU(N) on the periodic four-dimensional lattice, and the composition with Kanazawa’s Theorem 2. Conjecture: the closed form of the optimal constant for N ≥ 5. The quantity and the tool are classical (Tomboulis–Yaffe 1985; Kovács–Tomboulis 2002; Kanazawa 2008); an explicit bound at every coupling was not found in the texts we read (not a claim of absence). Nothing is said about the mass gap, about uniformity in the coupling or in the section, or about the neutral sector.

The rest is unchanged from version 1.1: a technical note on a sign-averaging inequality (multiplying by −1 all links of a column and averaging), twenty-three Lean 4 declarations including a bridge theorem on the lattice, the Wilson energy and the SU(2) of the public Lean development of OpenAI: for every period l ≥ 2 and β ≥ 0, |Z0 − Z1| ≤ tanh(β l2)l2 (Z0 + Z1); the tool is classical and no priority is claimed. A transfer-matrix consequence for a tube is proved on paper only. Written by AI models and read by other AI models; no human has checked the proofs; not refereed. The bounds degenerate when the transverse section grows at fixed β; they say nothing about the mass gap in dimension four, the weak-coupling regime, the continuum limit or the neutral sector.
